classify.label: Review
classify.prose: Hello! I hope you are doing well. I would really appreciate it if you could please read the customer review below and tell me whether its overall sentiment is positive, negative or neutral. Please reply with just that one word and nothing else, with no punctuation and no explanation. Thank you so much for your help!
classify.terse:
Classify the review's sentiment.
Reply with one word: positive, negative or neutral.
No other text.
classify.schema:
Task: sentiment of a review
Output: positive | negative | neutral
Format: one word, nothing else
classify.code:
def sentiment(review: str) -> Literal["positive", "negative", "neutral"]:
    """Overall sentiment of the review. Output the return value only: one word."""
classify.mixed:
Judge the overall sentiment of the review, as a careful reader would.
Output: positive | negative | neutral (one word, nothing else)
classify.abbrev:
Clsfy rvw sntmnt.
Rply 1 wrd: positive, negative or neutral.
No othr txt.

extract.label: Line
extract.prose: Hi there! Below you will find a single line taken from an invoice or a receipt. Could you please find the date and the amount of money in it for me? I need the date written as year, month and day in the form YYYY-MM-DD, and I need the amount as a plain number without a dollar sign or any commas. Please give me your answer as a JSON object that has the two keys date and amount, and please do not add any other words or explanation. Thanks a lot!
extract.terse:
Find the date and the amount in the line.
Return JSON with keys date and amount.
Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Amount as a plain number, no $ or commas.
JSON only.
extract.abbrev:
Fnd date & amt in line.
Rtrn JSON w/ keys date & amount.
Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Amt as plain nmbr, no $ or commas.
JSON only.

calculate.label: Figures
calculate.prose: Hello! I am trying to work out whether something is worth buying. Below I have listed the price of the item, how much money it saves me each time I use it, and the number of times I expect to use it. Could you please work out my net saving for me? That is the saving per use multiplied by the number of uses, with the price then taken away. Please reply with only the final number, without a dollar sign and without any explanation. Thank you very much!
calculate.terse:
Work out the net saving: saving per use times uses, minus price.
Reply with the number only. No $ and no explanation.
calculate.schema:
Task: net saving
Formula: saving_per_use * uses - price
Output: number
Format: number only
calculate.mixed:
Work out whether the purchase pays for itself.
net = saving_per_use * uses - price
Output: net (number only)
calculate.abbrev:
Wrk out net svng: svng per use x uses, mns price.
Rply w/ nmbr only. No $ & no explntn.

format.label: Note
format.prose: Hi! Below is a short note describing something I need to do. I would be grateful if you could please turn it into a JSON object for my to-do list. The object should have a key called title containing the task itself as text without the full stop at the end, a key called priority containing the priority as a whole number, and a key called tags containing a list of the tags as lower case strings. Please reply with the JSON object only and do not add anything else. Many thanks!
format.terse:
Turn the note into a JSON object.
Keys: title (the task, no final full stop), priority (whole number), tags (list of lower case strings).
JSON only.
format.schema:
Task: note to record
Output: {"title": string, "priority": integer, "tags": [string]}
Rules: title has no final full stop; tags lower case
Format: JSON only
format.code:
def to_record(note: str) -> dict:
    """Return {"title": str, "priority": int, "tags": list[str]}.
    Title has no final full stop. Tags are lower case.
    Output the return value only, as JSON."""
format.abbrev:
Trn note into JSON obj.
Keys: title (task, no fnl full stop), priority (whole nmbr), tags (list of lwr case strs).
JSON only.
